title: The Midnight Menagerie
subtitle: Crack the locks. Free the animals.
briefing: The sneaky collector Baron Bramble has stolen animals from the woodland sanctuary and locked them inside his castle. You found his secret gate. Follow the clues, outsmart his locks, and bring every animal home before sunrise.
setting: A make-believe castle. A very real need for your math skills.
finale: The last boat slips into the reeds just as the sun rises. All 12 animals are back at the woodland sanctuary. Baron Bramble finds empty pens, open locks, and one small note: Animals belong at home.

steps.title: The keeper’s code
steps.story: A brass lock blocks the entrance. Bramble has scratched three animal symbols above its dials. Peek through the bars and count each kind of animal.
steps.explanation: You counted 6 rabbits, 4 foxes, and 2 owls. In that order, they make the code 642.

clues.label: Field tip
clues.value: Tap an animal to mark it counted

puzzle.prompt: Set each dial to the number of that animal. Read the dials from left to right.
puzzle.hint: Count one kind at a time. Tap each animal once so you do not count it twice.

steps.title: A gap in the patrol
steps.story: The lookout turns away during part of each minute. Your team needs 10 seconds to cross. Set a delayed start so everyone clears the passage before the lookout turns back.
steps.explanation: The lookout turns back at 35 seconds. Subtract the 10-second crossing: 35 − 10 = 25. Leaving at second 25 gets everyone across exactly at second 35.

puzzle.prompt: What is the LATEST second you can start? Finishing exactly at second 35 is safe.
puzzle.hint: Work backward from second 35. Subtract the 10 seconds you need to cross.

steps.title: The carrot catch
steps.story: Six rabbits twitch their noses behind a food-powered latch. Each rabbit needs 2 carrots. Load just enough carrots into the feeder and the pen door will pop open.
steps.explanation: 6 rabbits × 2 carrots each = 12 carrots. Equal groups opened the first pen.

puzzle.prompt: How many carrots do you need altogether?
puzzle.hint: Add 2 six times, or multiply 6 by 2.

steps.title: The fox den cipher
steps.story: Four foxes are waiting at a padlocked den. A trail of numbered paw prints is the clue. Find the missing number, then turn the two lock dials.
steps.success: Four foxes join your rescue team!
steps.explanation: The paw-print numbers increase by 4 each time: 4, 8, 12, 16. The missing number is 16.

puzzle.prompt: Keep the pattern going. Set the dials to the next number.
puzzle.hint: Find the difference between 4 and 8. Add that same amount to 12.

steps.title: The moon tower lift
steps.story: Two owls are trapped in a lift basket. Balance the counterweight to lower them gently. Each owl weighs 3 kg, and the empty basket weighs 4 kg.
steps.success: Two owls flutter down. Every pen is empty!
steps.explanation: The owls and basket weigh (2 × 3) + 4 = 10 kg. The 4 kg and 6 kg weights balance the lift.

puzzle.prompt: Choose weights that exactly balance the owls AND their basket. Each weight can be used once.
puzzle.hint: First find the weight of both owls. Add the basket. Then choose weights with that same total.

steps.title: The missing bridge
steps.story: The animals follow you to a gap in the bridge. A winch needs the gap length in meters to lower a rescue plank. Six half-meter markings span the gap.
steps.success: The plank fits. Everyone crosses safely.
steps.explanation: 6 sections × 50 cm = 300 cm. Since 100 cm = 1 m, the gap is 3 meters long.

puzzle.prompt: How many meters long must the rescue plank be?
puzzle.hint: Multiply 6 by 50 to get centimeters. Divide that total by 100 to get meters.

steps.title: A tiny pit stop
steps.story: You count all 12 rescued animals in the reeds. One quarter of them need a drink before the last part of the escape. Put out one water bowl for each thirsty animal.
steps.success: Refreshed and ready for the river.
steps.explanation: One quarter means 1 of 4 equal groups. 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so you need 3 water bowls.

puzzle.prompt: How many water bowls do you need?
puzzle.hint: Split 12 animals into 4 equal groups. How many are in one group?

steps.title: The last boat home
steps.story: Your sanctuary guide has a boat with space for 5 animals per trip. The guide handles the return journeys. Plan enough trips from the castle bank to take all 12 animals home.
steps.explanation: Two trips carry only 10 animals. You need 3 trips: 5 + 5 + 2 = 12. The last trip does not have to be full.

puzzle.prompt: What is the FEWEST number of trips that can carry every animal home?
puzzle.hint: Count by fives until there is room for all 12. Remember the animals left after two trips.

introductionTitle: Twelve animals. One secret way out.
